6. Stretch: geostrophic balance at 250 hPa
Is a forecast's wind near jet level balanced the way the real atmosphere is? The ageostrophic fraction is |V − V_g| / |V|, the share of the wind that the geostrophic wind V_g (from the geopotential gradient) does not explain, taken over 30–70°N and averaged over the experiment's flights.
Done as an opt-in add-on with a reduced method (sections 7 and 8): NeuralGCM and its ensemble. The WeatherBench 2 NeuralGCM stores start on 2020-01-01 and have 12-hourly steps, so the add-on keeps only the flights with a NeuralGCM initialisation at every lead and plans every source from steps 12 h apart.
[FIG fig-geostrophic] 12 | 24 | 48 | 72 | 120 | 0.2 | 0.205 | 0.21 | 0.215 | IFS HRES | GraphCast | Pangu-Weather | ERA5 (reference) | Ageostrophic fraction at 250 hPa, 30–70°N, by lead time | lead time (h) | ageostrophic fraction (axis does not start at 0)
ERA5's ageostrophic fraction is about 0.21. The largest gap between any forecast source and ERA5 is 0.015. IFS HRES at 24 h sits just above ERA5.
7. NeuralGCM add-on: 5-source comparison
Reduced method: only the flights with a NeuralGCM initialisation at every lead (departures from 2020-01-06), and every source, not only NeuralGCM, planned from the steps at the lead and 12 h later (12-hourly planning), so differences between sources are not time-resolution differences. The add-on has its own candidate set (the truth-optimised plan and all five forecast sources) and its own results, separate from sections 1 to 5; the core experiment is unchanged. Lines are means and shaded bands are 90% CIs.
[FIG fig-neuralgcm] 0 | 100 | 200 | 300 | 400 | 500 | 600 | 12 | 24 | 48 | 72 | 120 | 0 | 2000 | 4000 | 6000 | 8000 | 12 | 24 | 48 | 72 | 120 | IFS HRES | GraphCast | Pangu-Weather | Persistence baseline | NeuralGCM | 5-source comparison on 6 flights, 12-hourly planning | lead time (h) | lead time (h) | mean fuel regret (kg) | mean fuel regret (kg) | Eastbound | Westbound | Forecast sources | Persistence baseline | Shaded bands: 90% CI of the mean
On 6 flights, NeuralGCM's mean fuel regret at the shortest leads (12-24 h) is 21 kg, rank 2 of the 4 forecast sources other than the persistence baseline, 3 kg above Pangu-Weather (18 kg); at the longest lead (120 h) is 130 kg, rank 3 of the 4 forecast sources other than the persistence baseline, 49 kg above GraphCast (81 kg). Planning 12-hourly instead of 6-hourly adds roughly 15 kg of mean regret at 12-24 h for IFS HRES, GraphCast and Pangu-Weather on the same flights, so short-lead numbers here mostly reflect time resolution, not forecast quality.
8. Ensemble robust plan (NeuralGCM ensemble)
On the add-on's flights and 12-hourly planning, a plan is made on each of M members of the NeuralGCM ensemble, and each plan is replayed through every member. The mean-robust plan has the lowest mean cost across members and the p90-robust plan the lowest 90th-percentile cost; each chosen plan is then replayed through the truth. Regret is floored at 0 against the add-on's hindsight plan, and the share of flights where a chosen plan beats it is reported. M is a subset of the 50 members, chosen from measured run time (cost grows with the square of M). The IFS ensemble and GenCast are not used: WeatherBench 2 stores them only at 500/700/850 hPa.
[FIG fig-ensemble] 12 | 24 | 48 | 72 | 120 | 0 | 50 | 100 | 150 | 200 | Mean-robust plan | p90-robust plan | NeuralGCM | GraphCast | Ensemble robust plans (M = 25 members), 6 flights, 12-hourly planning | lead time (h) | mean fuel regret (kg) | Shaded bands: 90% CI of the mean. Regret is floored at 0 against the NeuralGCM add-on hindsight plan.
The robust plans use M = 25 of the 50 members. At 120 h the mean-robust plan's mean fuel regret is 61 kg against 81 kg for the best deterministic source (GraphCast). Neither choice ever beats the add-on hindsight plan (0 of 60 plans). With M = 25 the 90th percentile is close to the maximum over members, so the p90-robust plan is overly cautious and costs more fuel (mean regret 90 kg at 120 h).
